questions.knowledge_point: Computing the Constant Term For the Fourier Series
questions.problem:
$$
f(x)∼\frac{{a}_{0}}{2}+{\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{a}_{n}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{n\pi }{3}x)+{b}_{n}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{n\pi }{3}x)
$$

Let $F(x)=4{x}^{2}-6x+3$ for $x\in [-3,3).$ The Fourier series of the $6$-periodic extension $f(x)$ of $F(x)$ is shown above. Find the exact value of ${a}_{0}.$

${a}_{0}=$ {{field-1}}
questions.worked_solution:
For the Fourier series of a $2L$-periodic function, the constant term is given by

$$
{a}_{0}=\frac{1}{L}{\int }_{-L}^{L}f(x)\,\text{d}x.
$$

In our case, $L=3$ and $f(x)=4{x}^{2}-6x+3$ for $x\in [-3,3).$ So, substituting into the formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{0} & =\frac{1}{3}{\int }_{-3}^{3}(4{x}^{2}-6x+3)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{3}{[\frac{4}{3}{x}^{3}-3{x}^{2}+3x]}_{-3}^{3} \\  & =\frac{1}{3}((\frac{4}{3}\cdot {3}^{3}-3\cdot {3}^{2}+3\cdot 3)-(\frac{4}{3}\cdot (-3)^{3}-3\cdot (-3)^{2}+3\cdot (-3))) \\  & =\frac{1}{3}(18-(-72)) \\  & =30.\end{aligned}
$$

$$

Let $F(x)=2{x}^{2}+7x+5$ for $x\in [-6,6).$ The Fourier series of the $12$-periodic extension $f(x)$ of $F(x)$ is shown above. Find the exact value of ${a}_{0}.$

${a}_{0}=$ {{field-1}}
questions.worked_solution:
For the Fourier series of a $2L$-periodic function, the constant term is given by

$$
{a}_{0}=\frac{1}{L}{\int }_{-L}^{L}f(x)\,\text{d}x.
$$

In our case, $L=6$ and $f(x)=2{x}^{2}+7x+5$ for $x\in [-6,6).$ So, substituting into the formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{0} & =\frac{1}{6}{\int }_{-6}^{6}(2{x}^{2}+7x+5)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{6}{[\frac{2}{3}{x}^{3}+\frac{7}{2}{x}^{2}+5x]}_{-6}^{6} \\  & =\frac{1}{6}((\frac{2}{3}\cdot {6}^{3}+\frac{7}{2}\cdot {6}^{2}+5\cdot 6)-(\frac{2}{3}\cdot (-6)^{3}+\frac{7}{2}\cdot (-6)^{2}+5\cdot (-6))) \\  & =\frac{1}{6}(300-(-48)) \\  & =58.\end{aligned}
$$

$$

Let $F(x)=x$ for $x\in [-3,3).$ The Fourier series of the $6$-periodic extension $f(x)$ of $F(x)$ is shown above. Find the exact value of ${a}_{0}.$

${a}_{0}=$ {{field-1}}
questions.worked_solution:
For the Fourier series of a $2L$-periodic function, the constant term is given by

$$
{a}_{0}=\frac{1}{L}{\int }_{-L}^{L}f(x)\,\text{d}x.
$$

In our case, $L=3$ and $f(x)=x$ for $x\in [-3,3).$ So, substituting into the formula, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{0} & =\frac{1}{3}{\int }_{-3}^{3}x\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{3}{[\frac{1}{2}{x}^{2}]}_{-3}^{3} \\  & =\frac{1}{3}(\frac{{3}^{2}}{2}-\frac{(-3)^{2}}{2}) \\  & =\frac{1}{3}(\frac{9}{2}-\frac{9}{2}) \\  & =0.\end{aligned}
$$
